claims.text: Near-equimolar quinary metal nanoparticles can initially form a single-phase solid solution.
Minor deviations from ideal atomic ratios locally diminish configurational entropy.
The effect of non-ideal atomic ratios becomes destabilizing above approximately 1000 K.
Reduced local configurational entropy enables partial phase segregation.
Elevated temperature can enable polymorphic structural transformations.
High configurational entropy associated with near-equimolar mixing stabilizes a solid-solution phase.
Local atomic size mismatch partially destabilizes high-entropy solid solutions at elevated temperatures.
Quinary nanoparticle systems with larger atomic size mismatch exhibit an earlier onset of phase segregation.
Quinary nanoparticle systems with larger atomic size mismatch exhibit more structural changes during thermal cycling.
Well-matched near-equimolar compositions remain largely single-phase and compositionally homogeneous over repeated 473–1923 K cycling.
A reference near-equimolar quinary alloy with minimal atomic size mismatch retains a single-phase solid solution throughout 473–1923 K.
Adequate dwell times at the target temperatures ensure near-equilibrium conditions.
The predicted size-mismatch effect holds under inert or mildly reducing conditions, controlled ramp rates, and absence of dominant mechanical or chemical stresses.
Defect states, local surface energies, and incomplete equilibration can obscure the relationship between size mismatch and phase stability.
A series differing systematically in atomic size mismatch can serve as a controlled comparison when subjected to the same 473–1923 K heating and cooling profile.
Failure to observe a consistent relationship between size mismatch and segregation onset or severity would falsify the proposed size-mismatch mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism identify deviations from equimolar composition and their effect on configurational entropy as the causal variable, whereas the intervention and mediator manipulate atomic size mismatch. No link is provided showing that size mismatch produces the stated local entropy reduction, so the experiment does not directly isolate the proposed compositional mechanism.
